A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that a relative localization algorithm for AUVs is locally weakly observable, which is the first time this property is shown for this kind of system.
, for the first time in the field of AUVs, the observability of the relative localization is analyzed and a nonlinear filter is developed.
we are able to provide a theoretical framework that allows to understand when and where we have observability and how to exploit it to improve localization of AUVs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observability of the system is ensured by a combination of the relative position measurements and depth measurements.
the depth sensors are crucial to achieve observability and the range measurements can be used to reduce the covariance of the estimation error.
, in the presence of a depth sensor, the observability properties are improved, thus reducing the requirements on the communication system.
